title: Engine Room: The Game of the Century
subject: A chess engine written from scratch reviews Byrne–Fischer, New York 1956 (the Game of the Century) move by move, with the search split across 8 Web Workers. Every part of its thinking is drawn live: the search tree, pruning, hash table, move ordering and threads.
why_hard: Everything is real and written by hand. Pieces: a legal chess engine in plain JS. The 0x88 move generator handles castling, en passant and promotion and is checked by perft up to 4,865,609 nodes. The search is PVS with a transposition table, null move, LMR, futility pruning and quiescence, and it has to reach depth 12–14 in 7 s per position. On top of that sits a root-split parallel search over 8 Web Workers that shares no memory. It uses speculative null-window scouts and re-searches, and it must stay exactly correct. The tree is instrumented live from inside the hot loop without killing the node rate. The screen draws a radial tree of about 2,500 nodes plus 11 other dense panels at 60 fps on an integrated GPU while 8 of the 16 threads run at 100%. The pieces are vector paths drawn by hand. No libraries, no images, no glyph fonts.
angle: Opus 5.5 at max effort, zero libraries: a hand-written chess engine, 8 Web Workers and raw canvas 2D, built in one night
science:
GAME (D. Byrne – R. Fischer, New York 1956, 0–1, 82 plies): 1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Bf4 d5 6.Qb3 dxc4 7.Qxc4 c6 8.e4 Nbd7 9.Rd1 Nb6 10.Qc5 Bg4 11.Bg5 Na4 12.Qa3 Nxc3 13.bxc3 Nxe4 14.Bxe7 Qb6 15.Bc4 Nxc3 16.Bc5 Rfe8+ 17.Kf1 Be6 18.Bxb6 Bxc4+ 19.Kg1 Ne2+ 20.Kf1 Nxd4+ 21.Kg1 Ne2+ 22.Kf1 Nc3+ 23.Kg1 axb6 24.Qb4 Ra4 25.Qxb6 Nxd1 26.h3 Rxa2 27.Kh2 Nxf2 28.Re1 Rxe1 29.Qd8+ Bf8 30.Nxe1 Bd5 31.Nf3 Ne4 32.Qb8 b5 33.h4 h5 34.Ne5 Kg7 35.Kg1 Bc5+ 36.Kf1 Ng3+ 37.Ke1 Bb4+ 38.Kd1 Bb3+ 39.Kc1 Ne2+ 40.Kb1 Nc3+ 41.Kc1 Rc2#. The moves are replayed by matching each SAN move against the engine's own generated legal moves, which is a second correctness check.

ENGINE: one JS source, used by the main thread for SAN, attack maps and SEE, and by the workers through a Blob URL. Board: 0x88 Int8Array(128) with piece lists, side to move, 4 castling bits, en-passant square and halfmove clock. Zobrist hashing uses two 32-bit halves seeded by xorshift32 and is updated incrementally in make and unmake. A move is an int32: from (7 bits), to (7 bits), promotion (3 bits) and flags (capture, en passant, castle, double push). Moves are generated pseudo-legally; a move is legal if the king is not attacked after make. Perft self-test at load:
- start position, d1–5: 20 / 400 / 8,902 / 197,281 / 4,865,609
- Kiwipete 'r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq -', d1–4: 48 / 2,039 / 97,862 / 4,085,603
- position 3 '8/2p5/3p4/KP5r/1R3p1k/8/4P1P1/8 w - -', d1–5: 14 / 191 / 2,812 / 43,238 / 674,624

EVAL: PeSTO tapered evaluation, using the mg/eg piece-square tables from the Chess Programming Wiki page 'PeSTO's Evaluation Function'. Material mg/eg: P 82/94, N 337/281, B 365/297, R 477/512, Q 1025/936. phase = N + B + 2R + 4Q (at most 24). e = (mg·phase + eg·(24 − phase))/24, plus 30 for the bishop pair and 10 for tempo. Centipawns, relative to the side to move.

SEARCH (each worker): iterative deepening with fail-soft negamax PVS.
- TT entry = 4 Int32: key32, move, depth|bound|age, score (mate scores adjusted by ply). Replacement prefers greater depth, unless the stored entry is from an older search.
- Check extension: +1.
- Null move when not in check, d ≥ 3, the side has non-pawn material and static eval ≥ β: R = 3 + ⌊d/6⌋.
- LMR for quiet, non-killer moves with index i ≥ 3 at d ≥ 3: r = ⌊0.75 + ln d · ln i / 2.25⌋. Re-search at full depth if the reduced search beats α.
- Futility at d ≤ 2: skip quiet moves when static + 100·d ≤ α.
- Quiescence: stand pat, then MVV-LVA captures and promotions. Captures with SEE < 0 are skipped. Delta margin 200.
- Move order: TT move > good captures (16·victim − attacker) > promotions > 2 killers per ply > history h[side][from][to] > bad captures. History update on a cutoff: +d² for the cutoff move and −d² for quiets tried before it, as h += b − h·|b|/16384.
- Mate score: 32000 − ply.

PARALLEL ROOT SPLIT: the coordinator runs on the main thread; each worker has its own private TT. Depths 1–4 run on one worker. For each depth d ≥ 5:
1. Order the root moves by the last iteration: best move first, then by subtree nodes.
2. PV job: the best move with an aspiration window s_prev ± δ, δ = 25 cp, doubled on each fail, ±∞ after 3 fails.
3. Send every other move at once as a null-window scout at α_s = (K-th best previous score) − δ, with MultiPV K = 3.
4. A scout that returns v ≤ α_s is resolved once the final α ≥ α_s; otherwise it is re-scouted at α.
5. A scout that returns v > α gets a full-window re-search that gives an exact score; if that score is above α, the move becomes the new best.
6. The move actually played in the game is always searched to an exact score.
7. The iteration ends when every root move is resolved.
Idle workers prefer moves they owned in the last iteration, so their TT is still warm; otherwise they take any pending job. Each job carries a deadline that the worker checks every 2,048 nodes. The coordinator does not start a new depth if elapsed + EBF·t(d) > movetime (7,000 ms).

INSTRUMENTATION: every 50 ms each worker posts its node and qnode counts, seldepth, current move stack, counters, and tree deltas for plies ≤ 4. A delta holds the path, subtree nodes added, score, node type (PV if inside the window, CUT if ≥ β, ALL if ≤ α), the index of the cutoff move and the legal-move count. Pruned siblings at a CUT node = legal − index − 1. Tree drawing: angular span ∝ √nodes among siblings; dot radius = 1.5 + 1.2·log10(nodes) px; rings at r = 80 / 165 / 245 / 320 px.

SCHEDULE: at load, one worker runs the perft self-test while the others run a quick pass over all 83 positions at depth 7, capped at 3 s. The deep pass then starts at ply 27 (after 14.Bxe7) with 7 s per position. That puts the position after 17.Kf1 (Black to move; Fischer played 17...Be6) at about 45–52 s after load.

NUMBERS:
- nodes: make() calls including quiescence, summed over all workers.
- nps: Σnodes / think wall time, measured with performance.now() in each worker.
- depth: last fully resolved iteration. seldepth: deepest ply reached, including quiescence.
- EBF(d) = nodes(d) / nodes(d−1).
- hashfull: ‰ of current-age entries among the first 1,000 TT slots.
- TT hit %: key matches / probes.
- first-move cut %: β cutoffs on the first move searched / all β cutoffs.
- null cut %: null-move searches that reached β / null-move searches tried.
- LMR re-search %: reduced searches that beat α / reduced searches.
- score: centipawns for the side to move in the log; White-relative on the eval bar and the graph.
- Wp = 1/(1 + 10^(−cp/400)) fills the eval bar; the graph plots 2Wp − 1.
- mate N = ⌈(32000 − |s|)/2⌉.
- CPL = max(0, s_best − s_played) from the mover's point of view, clipped at 1000.
- Verdict classes by CPL: best ≤ 10, excellent < 20, good < 50, inaccuracy < 100, mistake < 300, blunder ≥ 300.
- '!!' = CPL ≤ 10 and the opponent's best capture after the move gains ≥ 300 cp by SEE (a sacrifice the engine agrees with). '!' = only move (the second-best move is ≥ 150 cp worse).
- ACPL: mean CPL per side over the deep-analysed plies.
- Square digits: white attackers − black attackers.
- Machine numbers come from the kit; FPS and frame time come from requestAnimationFrame deltas.

design.layout: Analysis-workstation grid on the 1920×1080 stage with 8 px margins and gutters: three columns (board 560 | search tree 792 | instruments 536) above a 276 px bottom band. It reads left to right like an engine GUI: the position being thought about, then the brain (the radial search tree, the hero), then the engine's instruments, with the whole game's timeline and the machine along the bottom. Every rectangle is filled edge to edge, and the tree's circle has corner insets so no corner is empty.

design.fonts: Bahnschrift for panel titles, chips and big numerals (SemiCondensed and SemiBold instances). Cascadia Mono for every number, the UCI log and the SAN notation, 9–11 px with tabular figures. Segoe UI Variable for small labels and axis captions, 9–11 px. Pieces are vector paths, not glyphs.
design.feel: A grandmaster's analysis room after midnight. Board squares are maple #E6CDA0 and walnut #A8744C, pieces are ivory #F4EAD5 and ebony #2A211A, and the numerals look like brass instruments. The density is that of a many-pane engine GUI crossed with a trading terminal. The search tree is drawn like the growth rings of a walnut cross-section: plies are rings, 8 coloured worker paths crawl outward, and the principal variation runs through it like a pale-gold vein. Serious, warm and very dense, glowing on near-black brown.

panels.name: Top bar
panels.shows: Studio mark 'CLAUDE STUDIO · 001', title ENGINE ROOM, header 'D. Byrne – R. Fischer · New York 1956 · 0–1'. Live chips: ply n/82, side to move, think clock x.x/7.0 s, depth/seldepth, total nodes, nps, '8 workers / 16 threads', perft ✓, wall clock

panels.name: Board
panels.shows: Maple and walnut board with hand-drawn vector pieces and coordinates in the corner squares. The last move is tinted. The engine's PV is drawn as 4 numbered pale-gold arrows that fade; the move actually played in the game is a dashed ivory arrow. Each square has a tiny attack-balance digit (green +, red −). The left eval bar is White's win probability with a score label. Below the board: the SAN PV, the static-eval breakdown (material, mg/eg PST, phase n/24, tapered total) and captured pieces

panels.name: UCI options
panels.shows: The engine's real parameters as spin boxes, sliders, a knob and checkboxes in 3 columns. They are wired into the engine and take effect from the next think. Below them, the perft strip: start d5 4,865,609 ✓ · Kiwipete d4 4,085,603 ✓ · pos3 d5 674,624 ✓, each with ms and Mnps

panels.name: Search tree
panels.shows: Hero panel. Radial tree of the current think over faint growth-ring circles for plies 1–4, each ring labelled with its node count. Dots are sized by log subtree nodes. Edges are coloured by node type: PV gold, CUT copper, ALL steel. Faint ticks show pruned siblings. The 8 workers' current lines move outward as coloured paths with glowing heads. Ply-1 labels read like 'Be6 +2.31 4.1M'. Corner insets: nodes per ply and cut-rate bars (top left); α/β aspiration gauge with depth, seldepth and fail count (top right); PV/CUT/ALL counts and pruned total (bottom left); best move by depth for this think (bottom right)

panels.name: Engine output
panels.shows: Scrolling UCI info lines in Cascadia Mono: depth, seldepth, multipv, score cp or mate, nodes, nps, hashfull, time and the PV in SAN. Fields are colour-coded: aspiration fail lines in orange, new best moves in green, bestmove/ponder lines between positions

panels.name: Root moves
panels.shows: Every legal root move with its rank, SAN, score (exact, or a ≤/≥ bound), a log-scale node bar with %, a badge for the owning worker, the last job type (PV, scout or re-search) and the depth resolved. The move played in the game is tagged PLAYED with its exact CPL

panels.name: Worker lanes
panels.shows: 8 lanes on a sliding 8 s axis, one block per root-move job, coloured by type (PV gold, scout steel, re-search orange, aborted grey) and labelled with the move. Iteration boundaries are thin vertical lines. Per-worker column: knps, nodes, busy %, TT fill ‰

panels.name: Ordering & hash
panels.shows: 64×64 history heatmap (from-square × to-square, log scale), killer moves for plies 1–8 and a TT occupancy heatmap by age. Stat column: TT hit %, hashfull ‰, first-move cutoff %, null-move cut %, LMR re-search %, q-node share, futility prunes, check extensions

panels.name: Game record
panels.shows: Byrne–Fischer in two columns. Each move shows the engine's verdict glyph (!!, !, ?!, ?, ??) in its class colour, a tiny CPL, the engine's best move and score when they differ, and the depth (d7 quick pass or d12+ deep). The current ply is highlighted and future moves are dimmed. Footer: ACPL per side and verdict counts

panels.name: Eval graph
panels.shows: Plies 0–82, White-relative 2·Wp−1 with maple fill above zero and walnut below. Quick-pass points are dotted and deep-pass points solid. Verdict markers sit on the curve, depth bars per ply run under the axis, plus the analysis cursor and ±1/±3/±10 pawn ticks

panels.name: Iterations
panels.shows: One row per depth of the current think: d, ms, nodes, knps, EBF, score, aspiration fails, best move, PV head; the active row pulses. Mini charts: log10 nodes vs depth, and score by depth with best-move changes marked

panels.name: Machine
panels.shows: Measured by the kit: CPU % sparklines for the 16 logical threads in a 4×4 grid (the 8 workers visibly pin threads; no thread mapping is claimed), RAM used of 15.3 GB, GPU %, disk read/write MB/s, page FPS and a frame-time histogram with the 16.7 ms line, JS heap and total TT memory

mid_work: Recording starts 30 s after load. By then the perft self-test has passed and the depth-7 quick pass has filled the eval graph and verdicts for all 82 plies. The deep pass has finished plies 27–29 and is 6 s into ply 30, with 16.Bc5 to play. So the log already holds hundreds of info lines, the iteration table shows depths 1–12, the lanes show 8 s of jobs, the heatmaps are saturated, and the machine charts have 30 s of history with 8 threads pinned. The 'prewarm' is the perft self-test, the quick pass and the deep pass all starting the moment the page loads, with no intro screen; the 30 s recorder warm-up hides all of it. 17.Kf1 reaches the board at about t = 15 s, and the 7 s think on Fischer's 17...Be6 fills the tree during the dive.

post_angle: Day 1 of pushing Claude to the edge. Overnight, Opus wrote a chess engine from scratch with no libraries, plus a live window into its brain, and set it to review the Game of the Century (Byrne vs Fischer, 1956). 8 workers, {nps_peak} positions a second, {nodes_total} in all, depth {depth_max}. The hook is the 13-year-old Fischer's queen sacrifice, 17...Be6!!. If be6_found_depth > 0: it locks onto the move at depth {be6_found_depth} and scores it {be6_eval_cp} cp for Black. If it is 0: it did not find the move in 7 seconds, and Fischer did at 13. Every number on screen is computed live.
